provenance_note: Codex fallback research after Claude quota. Search snippets and repository README claims are recorded as such; no external code was installed or run. Source claims are paraphrased; official guidance is not a legal compliance opinion.

external_sources.title: FTC Policy Statement Regarding Advertising Substantiation
external_sources.creator: Federal Trade Commission
external_sources.inspected: official web page, reasonable basis and prior substantiation sections
external_sources.supports: Objective express and implied advertising claims need a reasonable evidentiary basis before dissemination; the level depends on the claim and its communicated support.
external_sources.limits: US policy context; not a legal review of a real campaign. Does not prove any marketing tactic works.

external_sources.title: Bringing Dark Patterns to Light
external_sources.creator: FTC staff
external_sources.inspected: official 48-page PDF text, pages 3 and 20-22 on false scarcity, baseless countdowns and hidden information; remainder not read
external_sources.supports: False countdowns, buried material terms and disguised advertising are among the patterns FTC staff flags as impairing choice.
external_sources.limits: Report is a policy and enforcement synthesis; packet does not certify a specific interface as unlawful.

external_sources.title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
external_sources.creator: FTC staff
external_sources.inspected: official page sections on honesty, material connections and results
external_sources.supports: Endorsements should be honest and not misleading; relevant material connections should be disclosed; a testimonial cannot replace evidence for objective outcomes.
external_sources.limits: Staff guidance is context-sensitive and not a safe harbor. The fictional offer has no testimonial.

external_sources.title: Advertising FAQ's: A Guide for Small Business
external_sources.creator: Federal Trade Commission
external_sources.inspected: official page claim-support and guarantee Q&A
external_sources.supports: Material product claims need evidence before running; testimonials or guarantees do not substitute for substantiation.
external_sources.limits: US general business guidance; claim-specific evidence requirements vary.

external_sources.title: Dark commercial patterns
external_sources.creator: OECD
external_sources.inspected: official abstract and bibliographic details; full 96-page report not read
external_sources.supports: OECD frames dark commercial patterns as interface practices that steer, deceive, coerce or manipulate consumer choices against their interests.
external_sources.limits: Abstract-level use only; no effect size or specific marketing-architecture conclusion taken from report.

external_sources.title: Best Practices for Survey Research
external_sources.creator: American Association for Public Opinion Research
external_sources.inspected: official page questionnaire-design and respondent-burden sections
external_sources.supports: Ask specific single-concept questions, avoid wording that pushes answers, consider response-option completeness and respondent burden.
external_sources.limits: Guidance does not validate this packet’s untested instrument or its sample.

external_sources.title: Learning about users and their needs
external_sources.creator: GOV.UK Service Manual user research community
external_sources.inspected: official page research methods, assumptions and validation sections
external_sources.supports: Use evidence and actual/likely user research to learn needs; internal opinions should be treated as assumptions for testing.
external_sources.limits: Government-service context; transfer to marketing audience research is a methodological analogy.

Audience, traffic, benefit, objection and CTA procedure; common social-proof and guarantee section templates.

Value proposition, trust, objections and experiment ideas; conversion-focused default.

Existing channel structure; packet adds claim consistency rather than a replacement playbook.

user_sources.use: Kyle reflective synthesis on ethos/pathos/logos, framing, kairos, canons and fallacies; not validated UX metrics.
Coursework signage scenario, not a current client proof.
Comparative appeal analysis; campaign and medical claims unverified and not reused.
Context, empathy, survey neutrality and attributed PCEA leads, not current audience evidence.
